summary: Solid, production-plausible logging architecture: durable buffer for spike absorption, deterministic worker pipeline as the PII boundary, hot search index for low-latency queries, and object storage/Parquet for cheap retention and exports. Versioned policies/schemas with raw preservation enables auditable reprocessing, and the failure-mode story generally matches the stated SLOs.
strengths: Clear PII enforcement boundary before index/tail, with auditable policy/schema versioning and raw retention for reprocessing
Good scalability primitives (buffer partitions, stateless workers, index lifecycle + mapping guardrails) and pragmatic DR/snapshot approach
weaknesses: Single "Log API" doing ingest + query + tail + export concentrates blast radius and scaling concerns (especially tail fanout and query isolation under load)
Some scale-critical details are underspecified (exactly-once/duplication handling end-to-end, per-tenant isolation in the search index, and operational limits for Kafka-to-SSE/WebSocket tailing)
